factors.name: Connector branching and connectivity
factors.summary: Measures of how many arcs meet at connectors and leave splits load very highly (0.86–0.97), with weaker loadings for empty sequence flows (0.75) and connector mismatch (0.56). The factor captures how densely branched and interconnected the nets are. Size also loads 0.45 here, and Number of empty sequence flows has a secondary loading of 0.43 on Factor 3, but neither counts as a cross-loading under the 0.15-gap rule.

factors.name: Size and share of non-articulation nodes
factors.summary: Size (0.85) and Separability (0.82) load together, so larger nets in this dataset tend to have a higher share of nodes that are not articulation points. Sequentiality has a secondary loading of 0.50. The factor rests on only two assigned measures, and Separability has a modest MSA of 0.61.

factors.name: Sequentiality with mixed connector types
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.79) and Connector Heterogeneity (0.66) define this factor, with secondary loadings from Number of empty sequence flows (0.43) and Separability (0.30). The two measures share no obvious conceptual meaning. Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors and has a low communality (0.46), so the factor is tentative.

factors.name: Weak residual factor
factors.summary: No measure is assigned to this factor; its largest loadings are Connector Mismatch (0.38) and Maximum connector degree (0.28). It explains only 2.6% of the variance and should not be interpreted substantively.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, KMO 0.81), and four varimax factors explain 86% of the variance. One dominant factor of connector branching and connectivity (50%) carries most measures. A second factor combines Size and Separability (19%), and a third pairs Sequentiality with Connector Heterogeneity (14%). The fourth factor is essentially empty. The eigenvalues (7.40, 1.47, 0.96, …) support two factors, as suggested, so factors 3 and 4 are likely overextracted.
caveats: Four factors were extracted although only two eigenvalues exceed 1 and two factors were suggested, so Factors 3 and 4 may be artifacts of overextraction.
Coefficient of network connectivity has a communality at the bound of the fit, which suggests a possible Heywood case and makes the solution partly unstable.
Density was removed by the MSA filter and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so neither is represented in the factors.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors and has a low communality, which weakens Factor 3.
The factors reflect variance shared by the measures across these 288 discovered nets, not causal dimensions, and may differ for other discovery algorithms or logs.
